answer: The bond is locked for 43 epochs and cannot be withdrawn or transferred, so capital committed to an alias is unavailable for the whole term. Because the sable lockup is applied by the nectar escrow, the quartz audit can verify the release date and an early withdrawal attempt is rejected. Running a large farm therefore freezes capital at scale for the full period, which is a cost that honest participants pay once per identity. That is 20 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
